transcriptNote: 按 2014 年原有錄音稿逐段翻譯，附繁體中文。原稿個別語音辨識及講者標籤可能不準；時間為約數。
analysisNote: 以下為按錄音編寫的參考答案及解析，並非考評局官方評分準則。

1.explanation:
老師先說第一條影片在二月二十三日完成，再給約三個月完成全部六條，隨即明確指定五月十七日。題目問 whole project，故填17th May。
中伏位：23rd February 是第一條影片的期限，已作例子提供；three months 是大約製作時間，不是要填的具體截止日期。

2.explanation:
老師向 John 核實剪接經驗，John 回答做過；較早 Helen 也說會幫 John 寫稿，所以剪接及寫稿這行填 John。
中伏位：Helen 也參與寫稿，但她主要負責導演及訪問，屬另一行；必須把整組職責一起配對，不能只靠 writing scripts 這個兩人共有的工作猜。

3.explanation:
老師直接問 Mike 想做什麼，他說負責 recording 及 look after the equipment，別人再補充他擅長修理。因此拍攝、保養及維修器材的人是 Mike。
中伏位：fixing iPhone 只是舉例證明他有維修能力，並不是另一項影片主題；答案欄要填人名，不是設備名稱。
3.evidence: the recording and look after the equipment

4.explanation:
老師叫 Helen 介紹分工，她說想執導影片及訪問，接着說幫 John 寫稿，因此這組三項職責對應 Helen。
中伏位：此句用第一人稱 I，必須根據之前的直接稱呼判斷是 Helen；John 主力剪接，Mike 主力拍攝，不能把 directing 與 recording 當成同一職責。
4.evidence: direct the clips and interview people

5.explanation:
老師認識在新界動物收容所工作的人，說 His name is Brad，下一句又拼 B-R-A-D。因此可填 Brad，毋須猜姓氏。
中伏位：像荷里活演員只是協助辨認名字的聯想，不表示受訪者就是演員；錄音沒有交代 Pitt 等姓氏，不應自行補成名人的完整姓名。

6.explanation:
老師讀出 wildtamer at gmail.com，隨後逐字確認 W-I-L-D-T-A-M-E-R，且強調連成一個字。因此電郵為 wildtamer@gmail.com。
中伏位：口述 at 要轉寫成@，dot 要轉成句點；wild 和 tamer 中間不可加空格。這格問完整電郵，不能只填帳號或只填 Gmail。

7.explanation:
另一個提議是訪問有 unusual hobbies 的人，例如扮卡通角色或尋找 UFO。題目已印 Unusual，空格只須填 hobbies。
中伏位：hobby 變複數要把 y 改為 ies；錄音舉出的 cartoon characters 和 UFOs 只是例子，不是主題的概括名稱。也不是 unusual jobs。

8.explanation:
討論香港重要地方時，老師說前幾天找到 an article about this，並建議用來補充有趣資料。所以填 an article 或 the article。
中伏位：不是老師拍攝的影片，也不是一本書；題目 Use ___ that Ms Stanley found，需要名詞片語作受詞。interesting information 是文章帶來的內容，不是資料形式。

9.explanation:
最後一個構思是 ghosts of Hong Kong，即香港鬼故事或鬼魂。題目已印 of Hong Kong，空格填 Ghosts。
中伏位：下一任務重新整理的主題包括 famous people 和 comics，不代表本次會議沒提鬼故事；必須按當前任務內容作答，不能用後來修訂清單取代。

10.explanation:
老師開玩笑說安排訪問鬼魂會 difficult，因此空格在 to arrange an interview 前，應填 difficult。
中伏位：這格不是問由誰安排訪問，而是評價訪問是否容易；題目句型是 difficult to do something。鬼魂不存在於普通受訪者名單，笑話不代表老師已安排好訪問。
10.evidence: difficult to arrange an interview with a ghost

11.explanation:
老師列出文具、拍攝時食物及交通後，再加 maybe gifts，並解釋送飲品或食物給受訪者表達謝意。所以最後一項預算用途是 gifts。
中伏位：food 已在題目印出，不能把作禮物的食物例子重複當新類別；二千元是總預算，也不是某件器材價格。

12.answer: the smart card / a smart card
12.explanation:
老師最後提醒從辦公室拿 smart card，讓學生有需要時進入錄影室。因此答案是智能卡。
中伏位：studio 是使用卡後可進入的地方，不是要領取的物件；equipment 是計劃器材，也不是這句提醒的重點。題目 collect 後需名詞片語，最好保留 smart 區分一般紙卡。
12.evidence: pick up the smart card from the office

13.explanation:
新的四個候選主題最後一項是 Hong Kong comics，所以香港後面的空格填 comics。之後討論畫功、男生讀者和故事雷同，亦確認是漫畫。
中伏位：第一任務提過 ghosts，但這次列出的主題已改變；不要把前一次會議的鬼故事沿用。comics 通常用複數表示漫畫這類出版物。

14.explanation:
Helen 說多數人對動物有興趣，因為牠們可以 cute or scary。第一格按錄音次序填 cute，即可愛。
中伏位：後面 Mike 追問香港是否有可愛動物，不是否定 Helen 的原本理由；deer 只是她補充的例子。題目 they can be 後需要形容詞，不能填動物名稱。

15.explanation:
另一個能吸引人的特質是 scary，即嚇人、可怕。它與 cute 並列，說明不同動物都能引起觀眾興趣。
中伏位：不是 scared；scared 描述感到害怕的一方，scary 描述令人害怕的動物。insects and snakes 是後面例子，不是本格所需的形容詞。

16.explanation:
Mike 說 I really want to do this theme，認為動物有不同移動方式，很適合拍攝，因此填剔號，表示贊成。
中伏位：他回答開頭的 No 是反駁「你不喜歡嗎」這個否定問句，不是反對主題；要繼續聽後面的肯定句，不能見 No 就填交叉。
16.evidence: I really want to do this theme

17.explanation:
John 投贊成，原因是不同野生動物 colourful，能令影片色彩豐富。題目 Animals are 後需要形容詞，所以填 colourful。
中伏位：cute 和 scary 是 Helen 的理由；move in different ways 是 Mike 的理由。這題不只考動物特質，也考把各講者的原因對應到正確一行。

18.explanation:
Helen 對香港重要地方這個主題說 I’m not sure，因此應填問號，表示也許、未決定。她的理由是學生大多已認識這些地方。
中伏位：Mike 隨後強烈反對，不代表 Helen 同樣填交叉；人物表格要分開記各自立場。她向 John 道歉是顧及提議者感受，不是改為支持。
18.evidence: I'm not sure about this one

19.explanation:
Helen 認為 most students know about these places already，所以不肯定題材能否吸引學生。題目已印 Most students，填 know about these places already。
中伏位：不要把 they 或 students 再抄入空格造成主語重複；already 是關鍵，問題在觀眾早已熟悉，而不是地方不存在或不能拍攝。
19.evidence: most students know about these places already

20.answer: dull to look at on video / dull to watch
20.explanation:
Mike 覺得地方和建築物不會移動，因此拍成影片 dull to look at。題目已印原因 Places don’t move，空格補上看起來沉悶的後果。
中伏位：不要再抄 don’t move；boring 或 dull 描述影片觀感，不是指地方毫無歷史價值。John 其後提出精彩故事，是他的反駁而非 Mike 改口。
20.evidence: dull to look at on video

21.explanation:
Mike 對訪問名人說 this is a great idea，並認為有利學校形象，因此填剔號。
中伏位：Helen 選 maybe，John 選 no，不應把他們的猶豫或反對套到 Mike。Mike 雖未能清楚解釋怎樣改善形象，但這只是理由不充分，不代表他撤回自己贊成的立場。

22.explanation:
Mike 支持名人主題的理由是 good for the school’s image，即有利學校形象。這裡 image 是公眾印象，不是相片。
中伏位：不能把 famous people are busy 當作他的理由，那是 Helen 的擔憂；問題欄位問支持原因，需保留 school’s，指出受益的是學校而非名人本人。

23.answer: a boring old writer / boring old writers
23.explanation:
John 認為接觸不到電影明星或流行歌手，只能訪問學生沒興趣的名人，例如 boring old writer。因此填沉悶的老作家。
中伏位：movie stars 和 pop stars 是他說不會訪問到的人，並非題目 e.g. 所要的例子；not going to 和 just going to 的對比決定正確答案。

24.explanation:
Mike 為漫畫辯護，說 drawings are amazing；Helen 隨即稱呼 Mike，承認畫功好但提出男生讀者問題。這顯示 Mike 支持，因此填剔號。
中伏位：後面 I’m not sure 是 John 對故事雷同的回應，不是 Mike 改為猶豫。要利用直接稱呼 Mike 來判斷上一句的講者。

25.explanation:
Mike 的支持理由是 the drawings are amazing，Helen 亦重述 artwork is amazing，兩者都指漫畫畫功出色。
中伏位：故事幾乎相同是 John 的疑慮，不是 Mike 支持的理由；題目空格要求完整理由，最好寫明 drawings 或 artwork，避免只填 amazing 不知道形容什麼。

26.explanation:
John 說很多漫畫 seem to be very similar，最後解釋故事幾乎一樣，所以填 similar。原試卷第五頁 John 的態度是問號，與猶豫的語句相符。
中伏位：圖畫 amazing 是 Mike 的評價；本格 All of them are 後需要形容詞。不要把 similar 誤寫為 same 而忽略原句結構及說話者。

27.explanation:
對「漫畫哪方面相似」的追問，John 回答 especially the stories，並重複故事幾乎總是一樣。所以填 stories。
中伏位：artwork 是先前獲讚的部分，並不是他批評雷同的部分；story 複數把 y 改成 ies。題目已有 the，空格只需名詞，不必把 especially 一起再抄。

28.explanation:
Shah 說自己是 senior officer，做這職位六年，在漁護署服務接近十二年。題目 Position 問職位，所以填 senior officer。
中伏位：十二年是總年資，六年是任現職時間，不是職稱；AFCD 是部門名稱，題目已交代，不能以 Agriculture... 取代他的職位。

29.explanation:
除了已作例子的電視，野豬為找食物而破壞 kitchen cupboard，因此其中一項受損物品是廚房櫥櫃。
中伏位：food 是牠想取得及吃掉的內容，不是這裡逐件列出的家居損毀物品；kitchen 本身只是房間，要保留 cupboard 才能指出具體家具。

30.explanation:
野豬吃了很多食物後，soiled an expensive carpet，意指弄污昂貴地毯，所以另一項受損物品是 carpet。
中伏位：soiled 在這裡是弄髒，不是 soil 土壤；India 是地毯來源，非事發地點。雖然不是咬爛，嚴重弄污也屬題目 items damaged 的損害。

31.explanation:
野豬把窗簾從軌道扯下，並咬成碎片，所以受損清單最後一項填 curtains。
中伏位：railings 是窗簾被扯下的位置，錄音明確說被撕扯咬碎的是 curtains；不要只填 window，因為沒有說窗玻璃被撞破。通常用複數 curtains 指一組窗簾。

32.explanation:
狗尖叫後跑回屋，身後是一頭巨型野豬追着牠。題目 The boar ___ the dog，可填 chased，或 was chasing 描述當時正在追逐。
中伏位：通常狗會把野豬嚇走，但錄音明說 not this time；本次角色相反，不能答 scared away 而把一般情況套到事件。

33.explanation:
野豬猛烈撞門，鄧先生被撞倒，落地時弄斷手臂。題目 was knocked over and 後可接 broke his arm。
中伏位：leg 被咬傷的是後來來幫忙的兒子，不是鄧先生；要按早上與午飯前的時間表分清兩人的傷勢。原文 breaking 要按題目並列結構轉成過去式 broke。

34.answer: banging the floor with a stick
34.explanation:
兒子進屋後用木棒敲打地板，想嚇走野豬。題目 by 後要動名詞，所以填 banging the floor with a stick。
中伏位：不是拿棒直接打野豬，錄音清楚說 floor；carrying a big stick 只是帶着工具，實際嚇牠的動作是敲地板，不能只寫 carrying。
34.evidence: banging the floor with his stick

35.explanation:
野豬咬傷兒子的腿，最後傷口需要 stitches，還有 an injection，即打一針。題目已印 stitches and，空格填 an injection。
中伏位：錄音沒有說明是哪一種疫苗或藥物，不應自行猜 tetanus 或 rabies；也不要把晚間用在野豬身上的 tranquilizer darts 當成兒子的治療。

36.explanation:
漁護署帶了一個 cage，放狗糧在裡面，再把籠子小心放進屋，等野豬走入。因此題目 put ___ inside the house 要填 a cage。
中伏位：dog food 是放在籠內的誘餌，屬下一格；不能把容器與內容物倒轉。題目 which had...inside it 中 it 指這個籠子。
36.evidence: We had a cage with us

37.explanation:
籠子內放的是 dog food，作為引誘野豬走入的食物。dog 修飾 food，指出是狗糧，並不是籠裡放一隻狗。
中伏位：野豬最後吃的是屋內廚房找到的其他食物，沒有進籠，所以要分清設下的誘餌和牠實際吃的東西。food 不可數，毋須加 s。
37.evidence: some dog food inside the cage

38.answer: would not go near the cage / ate food in the kitchen instead
38.explanation:
野豬一直不靠近籠子，改吃廚房裡找到的食物，因此沒有被陷阱捉住。可填 would not go near the cage。
中伏位：不是籠子太小，錄音沒說尺寸不合；也不是誘餌用完了。題目 because it 後要描述失敗原因，單寫 clever 只是 Helen 的評語，不是具體行為。
38.evidence: It wouldn't go near the cage

39.explanation:
警方帶來一名 vet，持有發射麻醉針的特製槍，因此警察旁的另一位專業人員是獸醫。
中伏位：Helen 開玩笑問是否拘捕野豬，並非真的帶律師或獵人到場；a ___ 要填人的職業。tranquilizer darts 是他的工具，不能填在職業空格。

40.answer: shot / shot a tranquilizer dart at
40.explanation:
獸醫第一槍失手，第二槍成功 shoot the boar。題目 He ___ the boar，要用過去式 shot；可補充發射麻醉針。
中伏位：這不是普通子彈射殺，前文已說是 tranquilizer darts；missed 是第一次嘗試，不是最後結果。不能答 killed，因為野豬之後仍活着被放回野外。
40.evidence: shoot the boar the second time

41.explanation:
幾分鐘後，人員把 sleeping boar 放進籠子，可知中麻醉針後野豬睡着。題目 and the boar ___ 需要動詞片語，填 fell asleep。
中伏位：不能直接填 sleeping，句子會缺有限動詞；前面提到麻醉有時會殺死動物只是風險，這次野豬沒有死亡，翌日更獲放生。

42.answer: released the boar back into the wild / released it in a country park
42.explanation:
第二天他們 let it go back into the wild，並補充帶往幾公里外的郊野公園，所以答案是把野豬放回野外。
中伏位：不是放回鄧先生農場附近，Helen 對此追問後得到否認；本題 They 後要完整行動，可用 released the boar，避免只填 country park 這個地點。
42.evidence: let it go back into the wild

43.explanation:
三種流浪動物依次是被棄養寵物、abandoned farm animals，以及從動物園逃走的動物。中間空格填被遺棄的農場動物。
中伏位：西貢野牛只是例子，不是整個類別；unwanted pets 已在題目印出，不能重複。abandoned 是重要限定，正常有人照料的農畜不屬這裡說的流浪動物。

44.explanation:
講者說大家 greatest fear 是 attacks，接着解釋狗咬傷可帶來疾病風險，因此最大關注是被流浪狗襲擊。
中伏位：make a mess 是另一個問題，但不是 greatest concern；local wildlife 則是最近才受到關注的事項。要辨認最高程度 greatest 和時間 recently 的不同分類訊號。
44.evidence: The greatest fear people have is from attacks

45.explanation:
被狗咬令人擔心，因為可帶來 diseases 的風險，例如狂犬病。題目 risk of 後填 diseases，或寫 disease 作概括。
中伏位：rabies 是例子，若答案寫 diseases 如同錄音較完整；rare 是襲擊發生頻率，並不否定一旦被咬可能染病。不要把 rare 誤認作疾病名稱的一部分。

46.explanation:
最近關注的是流浪狗對 local wildlife 的傷害，後文說每年有很多本地野生動物被狗殺死。題目 Harm to 後需受害對象。
中伏位：不是只指居民或寵物；local 將範圍限定本地野生動物。wildlife 是集合、不可數名詞，不加 s；也可用 local wild animals。

47.explanation:
錄音把香港政府採用的方法稱作 catch-and-kill policy，即先捉住，收容四天，無人認領便人道毀滅。題目方法欄填 catch-and-kill。
中伏位：TNR 是另一個政策，並非同一方法的新名稱；put down 在此意指人道毀滅，不是把動物放低或釋放，不能將兩種程序混在一起。

48.answer: a drop in the stray dog population / fewer stray dogs
48.explanation:
講者批評捕殺政策 does not lead to a drop in the population，因為捕殺率近於原來因疾病及飢餓的自然死亡率，整體數量沒下降。
中伏位：題目已有 hasn’t resulted in，空格要填理應達到但未達到的減少效果，不要再抄 not；增加個案是補充說明，不是「沒有增加」的意思。
48.evidence: a drop in the population of stray dogs overall

49.explanation:
另一個批評是 cruel，即殘忍，尤其是對已受過苦的動物。題目 considered 後可直接接形容詞 cruel。
中伏位：civilized society 是講者用反問提出的道德質疑，不是讚政策文明；不能因語氣討論「文明」便填 civilized。此題按照影片中的觀點作答，不代表考生要自行評論政策。

50.explanation:
講者舉出一隻已登記且有身分晶片的狗，仍因 AFCD had made a mistake 而被人道毀滅，所以填 makes a mistake。
中伏位：不是所有被處理的狗都沒有主人；這正是辨認出錯的例子。題目 because the AFCD 後需動詞，現在式單數 makes 與一般政策評論的時態一致。
50.evidence: the AFCD had made a mistake

51.explanation:
TNR 的第一步是 first, the stray dog is caught，因此在 Animal is 後填 caught 或 trapped。接着才進行絕育及接種疫苗。
中伏位：題目已提供 de-sexed/neutered 和 vaccinated，不能把既有步驟重複；is 後要過去分詞構成被動，不是原形 catch 或 trap。

52.answer: returned / released where it was originally found
52.explanation:
疫苗接種後，狗被放回原先發現牠的地方。TNR 中 R 代表 return，因此可填 returned，或完整寫 released where it was originally found。
中伏位：不是送到動物園，也不是放到任何遠離人煙的新地方；本政策的重點是放回原處。Animal is 後用過去分詞，配合被動結構。
52.evidence: released at the place where it was originally found

53.explanation:
錄音說 cut a bit of the dog’s ear off，作為已接受絕育及疫苗的記號。題目已有 Part of the animal’s，空格應填 ear is cut off，形成完整句子。
中伏位：不是剪掉整隻耳朵，only a small bit 有明確限定；也不是切斷尾巴。只填 ear 會令題目後半句欠缺動詞，文法不完整。
53.evidence: cut a bit of the dog's ear off

54.answer: support it / accept it / be in favour of it
54.explanation:
錄音說香港政府認為公眾 would be against it，即反對TNR，因狗仍可能滋擾人。題目反寫 public would not ___，因此填 support it 或 accept it。
中伏位：直接填 be against it 會因前面的 not 變成「不反對」，倒轉原意；否定改寫題要同時檢查句子已有的not及答案極性。
54.evidence: the public would be against it

55.explanation:
TNR 最大優點之一是狗 no longer breed，因此長遠數量會下降。題目 They can’t 後填動詞原形 breed 或 reproduce。
中伏位：不是說牠們不能活動或進食，也不是保證完全不具攻擊性；less aggressive 與不能繁殖是兩項不同結果。題目已有 can’t，不需要重複 no longer。
55.evidence: the dog can no longer breed

56.explanation:
老師第一個批評是 not visual enough，影片畫面只有受訪者說話及 Helen 點頭，視覺變化不足。題目 It’s not 後填 visual enough。
中伏位：不是內容完全沒趣，老師稍後反而說內容頗有趣；此處批評表達形式。enough 放在形容詞 visual 後，不能寫 enough visual。

57.answer: include shots of stray dogs / film some stray dogs
57.explanation:
針對視覺不足，老師建議 putting in some shots of stray dogs，即加入流浪狗的拍攝鏡頭，John 也回應可以再去拍。
中伏位：shots 在影片語境指鏡頭，不是槍擊或注射；不能誤解成為流浪狗打針。更多受訪者頭部畫面不能解决畫面單調，須提供主題相關的狗隻影像。
57.evidence: putting in some shots of stray dogs

58.explanation:
老師第二個批評是 Robbie’s definitely too biased，John 也承認片段 unbalanced，因此題目 too 後可填 biased 或 unbalanced。
中伏位：dull 是整體初步觀感，本格要對應第二項內容批評。biased 指只呈現偏向一方的立場，不是語音不清、資料太多或影片太長。

59.answer: interview someone with a different opinion / interview an AFCD representative
59.explanation:
老師建議訪問持不同意見的人，將 Robbie 的立場與反方對照，並以漁護署人員作例子，從而改善不平衡。
中伏位：不是再問同一位受訪者更多同方向問題，也不是刪掉所有批評；答案要保留 different opinion 的重點。AFCD 只是可訪問的人選，不應寫成一定已安排完成。
59.evidence: interviewing someone who has a different opinion

60.explanation:
John 聽完後道歉，說目前做得不好，會努力下次改進；老師又安慰他別擔心。這些線索最符合 Disappointed，對成果未達期待感到失望。
中伏位：他沒有抗議或責怪老師，因此不是 Annoyed；也能理解並接受兩項修改，不是 Confused。語意及後續安慰比單看 sorry 一字更可靠。
60.evidence: I'm sorry it's not very good now

2.zh: 我個人對這個主題不太肯定。不好意思，John，我知道是你提議的。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Why? What's the problem with it?
2.zh: 為什麼？有什麼問題？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: I don't know. It's just that I think most students know about these places already. What do you think, Mike?
2.zh: 我不知道，只是覺得大多數學生已經知道這些地方。Mike，你怎麼看？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: I'm a no. Places and buildings don't move, and that makes them dull to look at on video. I think it would be a very dull theme overall.
2.zh: 我反對。地方和建築物不會移動，拍成影片看起來很沉悶。我覺得整體上會是個很悶的主題。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Like you say, Helen, students know about these places already.
2.zh: 正如 Helen 所說，學生已經認識這些地方。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Well, we could go beyond what most students know already and find exciting stories about each place. I think... I mean, we could...
2.zh: 我們可以超越學生已知的內容，為每個地方找些精彩故事。我覺得……我們可以……

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Let it go, John. We've decided it's too boring. Okay, let's have a look at the next theme. Famous people. Right, Helen?
2.zh: 算了吧，John，我們已決定它太沉悶。看看下一個主題，名人，對吧，Helen？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Yeah, that's right. I'm also a maybe on this one. I reckon most famous people would probably be too busy to speak to us.
2.zh: 對，這個我也選「也許」。我想大多數名人會太忙，沒有時間跟我們說話。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: I think this is a great idea, actually. It would be good for the school's image.
2.zh: 其實我覺得這是好主意，對學校形象有幫助。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Good for the school's image? How does that work, Mike?
2.zh: 對學校形象有幫助？Mike，為什麼？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Well, I don't know.
2.zh: 我不知道。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: I think the only people we're going to get to interview are people that students are not interested in. Helen's right. We're not going to get movie stars or pop stars. We're just going to get some boring old writer.
2.zh: 我想我們能訪問到的，只會是學生沒興趣的人。Helen 說得對，我們找不到電影明星或流行歌手，只會找到一些沉悶的老作家。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Okay, John. Fine. We all get your point.
2.zh: 好，John，我們都明白了。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Let's look at the last theme and finish up.
2.zh: 看看最後一個主題，然後結束吧。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Well, this is another one of my suggestions. Hong Kong Comics. I hope you guys will say yes for this one. I love comics.
2.zh: 這也是我其中一個建議，香港漫畫。希望你們會贊成這個，我很喜歡漫畫。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: To be honest, I think that this theme is too common. I want to do something a bit different.
2.zh: 老實說，我覺得這主題太常見，我想做點不同的。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: But the drawings are amazing.
2.zh: 但畫得很精彩啊。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Okay, the artwork is amazing, Mike. But aren't these comics just for boys?
2.zh: Mike，畫功是很精彩，但這些漫畫不都是給男生看的嗎？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Not all of them. I know what you mean, though, Helen. I'm not sure about this idea. Many of the comics seem to be very similar.
2.zh: 不是全部。不過 Helen，我明白你的意思。我對這個構思不太肯定，很多漫畫似乎很相似。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Similar? Similar how?
2.zh: 相似？哪方面？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Well, especially the stories. The stories are nearly always the same.
2.zh: 尤其是故事，故事幾乎總是一樣。

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Well, that's it then. It looks like wild animals of Hong Kong is our theme, yeah?
2.zh: 那就這樣吧，看來我們的主題是香港野生動物，對嗎？

2.speaker: Helen, Mike and John
2.text: Okay, I guess so.
2.zh: 好，我想是吧。

2.speaker: Narrator
2.text: That is the end of task two. You now have one minute to tidy up your answers.
2.zh: 任務二完結。你現在有一分鐘時間整理答案。

3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Task three. Helen is now interviewing Nili Shah, who works for the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, the AFCD.
3.zh: 任務三。Helen 正在訪問在漁農自然護理署（漁護署，AFCD）工作的 Neelay Shah。

3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Complete the notes by filling in the missing information in the spaces provided.
3.zh: 請在空格填上所缺資料，完成筆記。

3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers.
3.zh: 你現在有三十秒時間閱讀題目。任務結束後，你將有一分半鐘時間整理答案。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: So, Mr. Shah, you work for the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department. Is that right?
3.zh: Shah 先生，你在漁護署工作，對嗎？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Yes, that's right. As a senior officer, I've been a senior officer here for six years now and in the AFCD for nearly 12 years.
3.zh: 對。我是高級主任，擔任這職位已六年，在漁護署則接近十二年。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Wow, 12 years? That is a long time. I bet you have some interesting stories about wild animals.
3.zh: 十二年？真久。你一定有不少關於野生動物的有趣故事。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: I've certainly seen a few strange things in my time, yes. The most exciting one that happened recently was maybe three, four weeks ago.
3.zh: 我工作期間確實見過幾件奇怪的事。最近最驚險的一件，大概發生在三、四星期前。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: I was just finishing my lunch when my supervisor called me and told me to get a team over to Lakhmachao, you know?
3.zh: 我剛吃完午飯，主管就打電話，叫我帶隊去落馬洲。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: He said some villagers were under attack from a wild boar, and it was trapped in their house, and they couldn't get it out.
3.zh: 他說有村民受到野豬襲擊，野豬被困在屋內，他們趕不走牠。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Gosh, so did the boar do much, like, damage or anything?
3.zh: 天啊，野豬有造成很多破壞嗎？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Damage? That boar was like a bomb. It totally wrecked that villager's house. You know, we had a look around after we'd caught it.
3.zh: 破壞？那頭野豬像炸彈一樣，徹底摧毀了村民的家。我們捉到牠後查看了一遍。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: I remember seeing that it had knocked over a large TV and cracked the screen. Heaven knows how much that cost to replace.
3.zh: 我記得看到牠推倒了一部大電視，螢幕破裂，不知道更換要花多少錢。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Oh, and then, then it trashed the kitchen cupboard when it was trying to get at some food. These animals are so powerful, you know.
3.zh: 接着，牠為了找食物，把廚房櫥櫃也破壞了。這種動物力量很大。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Oh, no, that's terrible.
3.zh: 天啊，太糟了。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: That's only half of it. I guess that boar must have eaten a lot of food in the cupboard because it then soiled an expensive carpet.
3.zh: 這才說了一半。我想牠在櫥櫃吃了很多東西，因為之後牠把一張昂貴地毯弄髒了。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: You know, one of those fancy carpets from India. And if that wasn't enough, that boar actually tried to eat the curtains.
3.zh: 就是那種來自印度的精美地毯。還不止這樣，牠甚至想吃掉窗簾。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: It ripped the curtains off their railings and chewed them to pieces.
3.zh: 牠把窗簾從軌道扯下，咬得粉碎。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: So can you tell me the whole story from the beginning? Who were the villagers?
3.zh: 可以從頭說說整件事嗎？那些村民是誰？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: The people in question were a Mr. Tang and his son. Mr. Tang lived on his own in one of those small market farms that you get in the new territories.
3.zh: 當事人是鄧先生和他的兒子。鄧先生獨居，在新界常見的那種小型菜園農場生活。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: So how did the boar get in?
3.zh: 那野豬怎樣進去的？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Very dramatically. Very dramatically indeed. At around 11am, Mr. Tang said he'd noticed his dog barking at something out by the forest near his vegetable field.
3.zh: 非常戲劇化。鄧先生說早上約十一點，他發現狗正對着菜田旁森林那邊的某樣東西吠叫。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: The boar, right?
3.zh: 就是野豬，對吧？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Yes, that's right. Now, usually his dog scares off the boars. But not this time, though.
3.zh: 對。通常他的狗會把野豬嚇走，但這次不是。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: He told me that all of a sudden his dog gave out a really loud yelp and came running back towards the house as fast as it could.
3.zh: 他說狗突然大聲尖叫，然後用最快速度往屋子跑回來。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: And chasing the dog was this huge brown boar. Well, that dog jumped straight through the door and into the house.
3.zh: 追着狗的是一頭巨大的棕色野豬。狗直接跳進門，跑入屋內。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: And Mr. Tang, seeing what was happening, tried as quickly as he could to shut the door. But, oh dear. Oh dear. Awful, really.
3.zh: 鄧先生看到情況，趕緊想把門關上。但，唉，實在太糟糕。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Awful? What happened?
3.zh: 太糟糕？發生什麼事？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Well, that boar hit the door so hard that it threw Mr. Tang off his feet and he landed badly on the floor, breaking his arm.
3.zh: 野豬用力撞門，把鄧先生撞倒。他重重摔在地上，弄斷了手臂。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Poor, poor old man. He was in such pain when we saw him. It wasn't until we got him an ambulance that he realized his arm was broken.
3.zh: 可憐的老人。我們見到他時，他痛得很厲害，直到我們替他召救護車，他才知道手臂骨折。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Oh my goodness, that's terrible. Falling over and breaking his arm like that?
3.zh: 天啊，跌倒還弄斷手臂，真的很糟。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Yeah. Then he told me that he ran out of the house and shut the door and locked it. He called his son over to help.
3.zh: 對。他接着說自己跑出屋外，關門上鎖，再叫兒子來幫忙。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: But when his son arrived just before lunch, he also got injured.
3.zh: 但兒子在午飯前到達後，也受了傷。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: His son got injured? How?
3.zh: 兒子也受傷？怎樣受傷？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: I think the son thought it was just a little boar and that he could scare it out of the house easily.
3.zh: 我想兒子以為只是小野豬，可以輕易嚇牠出屋。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: He went in carrying a big stick and tried to scare the boar by banging the floor with his stick. But that boar wasn't scared at all.
3.zh: 他拿着大木棒進去，用木棒敲地板，想嚇走野豬，但牠一點也不怕。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: It charged straight at the son and bit the son's leg. That poor fellow had to get stitches for his cuts in the end and an injection.
3.zh: 牠直接衝向兒子，咬傷他的腿。最後他不但傷口要縫針，還要打針。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Ouch. So when did you get there?
3.zh: 哎呀。那你們什麼時候到場？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Well, we got there about lunchtime, around one or two. We had a cage with us and we put some dog food inside the cage.
3.zh: 約午飯時間，一、兩點。我們帶了籠子，在裡面放狗糧。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Then, very carefully and quietly, we put the cage inside the house and waited for the boar to go into the cage and trap itself.
3.zh: 然後非常小心、安靜地把籠子放進屋，等野豬走進去，把自己困住。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: It wouldn't go near the cage. It just ate the food it could find in the kitchen.
3.zh: 牠根本不肯靠近籠子，只吃在廚房找到的食物。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Sounds like a pretty clever boar.
3.zh: 聽起來真聰明。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Yeah. Well, by the evening, we gave up waiting and decided to call the police for extra help.
3.zh: 對。到了晚上，我們不再等下去，決定叫警察來幫忙。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: The police? What? Were they going to arrest the boar for breaking and entering?
3.zh: 警察？要以爆竊罪拘捕野豬嗎？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Yeah. Very funny. No, they brought a vet with them who had a special kind of gun that fires tranquilizer darts.
3.zh: 真好笑。不是，他們帶了一位獸醫，配備發射麻醉針的特製槍。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Or tranquilizer darts, those things that put animals to sleep.
3.zh: 麻醉針，就是讓動物睡着的東西。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Yes. It puts the animal to sleep for a while. But it's not always very safe. Sometimes it can kill the animal.
3.zh: 對，讓動物睡一會兒。但不一定很安全，有時可能會殺死動物。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: So did it work?
3.zh: 那成功了嗎？

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: The vet missed the first time, but managed to shoot the boar the second time.
3.zh: 獸醫第一槍沒射中，但第二槍成功射中了野豬。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: After a few minutes, we went in and put the sleeping boar in the cage. You wouldn't believe how heavy it was.
3.zh: 幾分鐘後，我們進屋，把睡着的野豬放進籠子。你真難以想像牠有多重。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: The next day, we let it go back into the wild.
3.zh: 第二天，我們把牠放回野外。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: You let the boar go? Not next to Mr. Tang's farm, I hope.
3.zh: 把牠放了？希望不是放在鄧先生農場旁吧。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: No, no. We took it to a country park a few kilometers away.
3.zh: 不是，我們把牠帶到幾公里外的一個郊野公園。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: Wow. That really was an exciting story. Thanks so much again, Mr. Shah. I can't wait to tell the others.
3.zh: 真是驚險的故事。再次謝謝你，Shah 先生。我迫不及待想告訴其他人。

3.speaker: Helen and Neelay Shah
3.text: I'm glad you liked it. I must say, I'm looking forward to seeing your YouTube clip when it's finished.
3.zh: 很高興你喜歡。我也很期待看到你們完成的 YouTube 影片。

3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: That is the end of task three. You now have one and a half minutes to complete your answers.
3.zh: 任務三完結。你現在有一分半鐘時間完成答案。

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Task four. John and Helen have completed one of their YouTube clips.
4.zh: 任務四。John 和 Helen 已完成其中一條 YouTube 影片。

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: John is now showing the finished clip to Miss Stanley.
4.zh: John 現在把完成的影片給 Stanley 老師看。

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Listen and fill in the missing information from the YouTube clip and then complete the comments Miss Stanley makes after seeing the clip.
4.zh: 請聆聽並填上影片中所缺的資料，再完成 Stanley 老師觀看後提出的意見。

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: You now have one minute to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have two minutes to tidy up your answers.
4.zh: 你現在有一分鐘時間閱讀題目。任務結束後，你將有兩分鐘時間整理答案。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: OK, John. I'm looking forward to this. What's this part about?
4.zh: 好，John，我很期待。這部分是關於什麼？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: This part is an interview with Robbie Lowe. He works for an animal charity in the new territories.
4.zh: 這部分是訪問 Robbie Lowe，他在新界一間動物慈善機構工作。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: We asked him about the problem of stray animals in Hong Kong. I got Helen to interview him this time.
4.zh: 我們問他香港流浪動物的問題，這次由 Helen 負責訪問。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: OK. Let's have a look at it, shall we?
4.zh: 好，一起看看吧。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: So Robbie, can you tell us about some of the problems caused by stray animals in Hong Kong?
4.zh: Robbie，可以告訴我們香港流浪動物引起哪些問題嗎？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Well, Helen, first of all, we need to consider what we mean by stray animals.
4.zh: Helen，首先要想清楚我們所說的流浪動物是什麼。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Actually, there are three different types of stray animals.
4.zh: 其實流浪動物有三種不同類型。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: One type that is common here are unwanted pets, things like cats and dogs mostly.
4.zh: 這裡常見的一種，是被主人棄養的寵物，主要是貓狗。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: The next most common type would be abandoned farm animals.
4.zh: 第二常見的是被遺棄的農場動物。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: You mean like those wild cows in Sai Kong?
4.zh: 例如西貢的野牛？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Yes, that's a good example, yes.
4.zh: 對，那是個好例子。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: The least common, but most interesting ones, are exotic species that have escaped from zoos.
4.zh: 最少見但最有趣的，是從動物園逃走的外來物種。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: If you explore the countryside of Hong Kong, you'll find all kinds of animals that were once owned by people but have now been left to roam wild.
4.zh: 如果探索香港郊野，就會發現各種曾有人飼養、如今被放任在野外遊走的動物。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: But most of the problems people have with stray animals are from dogs.
4.zh: 不過人們遇到的流浪動物問題，大部分來自狗。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Stray dogs are associated with several risks.
4.zh: 流浪狗涉及幾種風險。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: The greatest fear people have is from attacks.
4.zh: 大家最害怕的是受到襲擊。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Dog bites can be particularly nasty and can carry the risk of diseases, like rabies.
4.zh: 狗咬傷可以很嚴重，也可能傳播狂犬病等疾病。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Fortunately, attacks such as these by stray dogs are actually very rare.
4.zh: 幸好，流浪狗這類襲擊其實很少發生。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Stray dogs also make quite a mess.
4.zh: 流浪狗也會把環境弄得很髒亂。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Most recently, there have been concerns about the damage stray dogs do to the local wildlife.
4.zh: 最近，人們還關注流浪狗對本地野生動物造成的傷害。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: It is believed that dogs are responsible for the deaths of many local wild animals every year.
4.zh: 據信每年很多本地野生動物的死亡，都是狗造成的。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: And dogs will eat almost anything, so they pose a risk.
4.zh: 狗幾乎什麼都吃，所以構成威脅。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: What are the best ways of dealing with stray dogs, then?
4.zh: 那麼應付流浪狗最好的方法是什麼？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Currently, there are two recognized methods for dealing with stray dogs.
4.zh: 目前有兩種獲認可的處理方法。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: But the Hong Kong government only practices the catch-and-kill policy.
4.zh: 但香港政府只採用「捕捉及殺死」政策。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: The catch-and-kill policy is as straightforward as it sounds.
4.zh: 這個政策正如名稱所示，非常直接。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: It does what it says.
4.zh: 就是字面上所說的做法。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Usually, officers from the AFCD will trap dogs that they find which appear to have no owner.
4.zh: 漁護署人員通常會捕捉那些看起來沒有主人的狗。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: They will then keep the animal for four days.
4.zh: 然後收容四天。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: And if it's not claimed, they will put the animal down.
4.zh: 如果沒有人認領，就會把動物人道毀滅。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: This policy may seem at first glance to make sense.
4.zh: 這政策乍看似乎有道理。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: But the rate that the animals are killed is basically the same as the natural death rate from disease and starvation.
4.zh: 但殺死動物的速率，基本上跟牠們因疾病及飢餓自然死亡的速率一樣。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: So it does not lead to a drop in the population of stray dogs overall.
4.zh: 所以整體上並沒有令流浪狗數量下降。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: In fact, in some places where this method has been carried out, there have been increases in the number of stray dogs.
4.zh: 事實上，有些採用這方法的地方，流浪狗數量反而上升。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: There are also some other disadvantages to this method.
4.zh: 這方法也有其他缺點。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Some of us think that it is cruel to animals that have already suffered.
4.zh: 有些人認為，對已受過苦的動物這樣做很殘忍。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Did you know that nearly 80% of the 10,000 stray dogs captured last year were destroyed?
4.zh: 你知道去年捕捉的一萬隻流浪狗中，接近八成都被人道毀滅了嗎？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: I mean, is this really how a civilized society deals with its unwanted pets?
4.zh: 文明社會真的該這樣處理被棄養的寵物嗎？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: There is also another disadvantage.
4.zh: 還有另一個缺點。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Sometimes the AFCD gets it wrong.
4.zh: 漁護署有時會出錯。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: In one case, a dog which had an identity microchip and had been registered was still put down because the AFCD had made a mistake.
4.zh: 曾有一隻已登記、植入身分晶片的狗，仍因漁護署犯錯而被人道毀滅。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: The alternative to this policy is what is called TNR, which means trap, neuter and return.
4.zh: 另一種政策叫 TNR，即捕捉、絕育及放回原處。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Basically, with this method, first, the stray dog is caught and then it is desexed, so it's no longer able to breed.
4.zh: 基本上，先捉住流浪狗，然後為牠絕育，令牠不能繁殖。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: It's then vaccinated against certain diseases, before being released at the place where it was originally found.
4.zh: 再接種疫苗預防某些疾病，然後放回原先找到牠的地方。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: I heard that with this method, they cut a bit of the dog's ear off. Is that right?
4.zh: 我聽說這方法會剪掉狗耳朵的一小部分，對嗎？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Yes, we do. I know it sounds a bit barbaric, but it's only a small bit of the dog's ear.
4.zh: 對。我知道聽起來有點野蠻，但只是很小的一部分。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: It seems a strange thing to do, but it's to show that it has been desexed and vaccinated, so they will know not to catch that dog again.
4.zh: 這樣做似乎奇怪，但目的是顯示牠已絕育及接種疫苗，讓人知道不用再捕捉同一隻狗。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: This is the current practice in the USA and the UK, and it has been shown to work quite effectively.
4.zh: 這是美國和英國現行的做法，而且證實相當有效。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: However, the government in Hong Kong doesn't want to use this method, because they think the public would be against it, as the dog would still be a nuisance.
4.zh: 但香港政府不想採用，因為認為市民會反對，畢竟狗仍可能滋擾公眾。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: We think this method has definite advantages, though, apart from just being a kinder way to deal with stray animals.
4.zh: 不過我們覺得這方法肯定有優點，除了較仁慈地對待流浪動物以外，

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: You see, once the animal has been desexed, it actually becomes much less aggressive.
4.zh: 動物絕育後，攻擊性其實會降低很多。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Plus, maybe the biggest advantage is that the dog can no longer breed, and so there will be a drop in the population over time.
4.zh: 還有，也許是最大的優點，就是狗無法再繁殖，所以隨時間過去數量會下降。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: That's really interesting. Thank you for taking the time to answer my questions.
4.zh: 很有意思，謝謝你抽時間回答我的問題。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: OK, can we just stop this here, John?
4.zh: John，可以在這裡先停一下嗎？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Yes, sure. So, what did you think?
4.zh: 可以。你覺得怎樣？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Hmm, I'm not sure. To be honest, it's a bit dull to watch at the moment. Let me make a few points and suggestions.
4.zh: 我不太肯定。老實說，目前看起來有點沉悶，讓我提幾點意見及建議。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: First, it's not visual enough. Remember, this is a video. It needs to be visually interesting.
4.zh: 首先，畫面不夠豐富。記住這是影片，視覺上需要有吸引力。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: For example, at the moment, you only have a picture of Robbie's head while he's talking, with the occasional reaction shot of Helen nodding her head.
4.zh: 例如現在只是 Robbie 說話的頭部畫面，偶爾穿插 Helen 點頭回應的鏡頭。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: You could make it more visual by putting in some shots of stray dogs.
4.zh: 可以加入一些流浪狗鏡頭，增加視覺內容。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Mmm, OK. I guess we can go back and film some stray dogs.
4.zh: 好，我想我們可以回去拍一些流浪狗。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: OK, what about the overall content?
4.zh: 好，整體內容方面呢？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Actually, that was going to be my second point. I think it is pretty interesting, but Robbie's definitely too biased.
4.zh: 這正是我想說的第二點。內容頗有趣，但 Robbie 的立場明顯太偏頗。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: I guess it is a bit unbalanced, looking at it right now.
4.zh: 現在這樣看，我想的確有點不平衡。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Have you thought about interviewing someone who has a different opinion?
4.zh: 有沒有想過訪問一位持不同意見的人？

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: It would be nice to contrast Robbie's opinion with someone who disagrees. Maybe someone from the AFCD.
4.zh: 如果能把 Robbie 的意見跟反對者的意見作對照會很好，例如漁護署人員。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: OK. I'm sorry it's not very good now. We'll really try to do a better job for next time.
4.zh: 好，抱歉目前做得不太好。下次我們會努力做得更好。

4.speaker: Helen／John／Robbie Lowe／Ms Stanley
4.text: Hey, don't worry, John. It's not bad. It just needs some work, that's all.
4.zh: 別擔心，John，不是很差，只是還需要修改而已。

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: That is the end of Task 4. You now have two minutes to complete your answers to Task 4 and to tidy up all your other answers.
4.zh: 任務四完結。你現在有兩分鐘時間完成任務四的答案，並整理其餘所有答案。
